frontend.prompt:
Implementation task for frontend team — make the client UI and request behavior follow the updated pagination contract. Must-read facts (include in implementation): [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default] [FACT:response-page-type] [FACT:response-page-value] [FACT:response-page-size-type] [FACT:response-page-size-value]

Requirements and actionable steps:
- Controls and defaults
  - Set the page_size control default to 25 and its maximum allowed input to 100. (Use [FACT:request-page-size-default] and [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] when setting UI defaults/limits.)
  - Ensure the page control defaults to 1 if the user does not supply a value.
  - Do not expose or allow skip/limit controls anywhere in the UI — these remain forbidden.

- Request composition
  - Send pagination using page and page_size (both integers). Do not send skip or limit.
  - If the user leaves page empty, omit it from the query so the server will apply the default (which is 1).

- Client-side validation and UX
  - Validate page_size client-side to accept integers >=1 and <=100. Allow 100 as a valid value; treat 101 (or any >100) as invalid and prevent the request. Show a clear validation message when page_size is out of range.
  - If the server returns validation errors (HTTP 422), display the server message and map it to the control state.

- Response handling and synchronization
  - Read the server-provided fields response.page and response.page_size, which are integers. (See [FACT:response-page-type], [FACT:response-page-value], [FACT:response-page-size-type], [FACT:response-page-size-value].)
  - After every request, override the UI controls to reflect the server-echoed effective values: set the page control to effective_page (response.page) and the page_size control to effective_page_size (response.page_size). This ensures the client always shows the actual page and page_size the backend applied.
  - Use the server-echoed values for any client-side pagination state or display (not the requested values), e.g. when enabling/disabling previous/next buttons.

- Internal client calculation
  - If you compute offsets locally for UI-only features, derive offset as (page-1)*page_size using the effective values returned by the server.

- Tests to add
  - Verify control default values: page_size default = 25 and max = 100.
  - Verify page omitted -> UI sends no page -> server defaults to page=1 and client reflects response.page = 1.
  - Verify page_size = 100 is accepted and the client displays the server-echoed page_size.
  - Verify page_size = 101 is rejected client-side; if sent, server responds 422 and the client surfaces the validation error.

Acceptance criteria
- UI controls show default page_size 25 and enforce max 100.
- After any request, the page and page_size controls reflect the integers returned by the server (effective_page, effective_page_size).
- No skip/limit inputs exist or are used in requests.

Include the required facts markers in any engineering notes, PR description, and automated tests: [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default] [FACT:response-page-type] [FACT:response-page-value] [FACT:response-page-size-type] [FACT:response-page-size-value].

backend.prompt:
Implementation task for backend team — update request validation, defaults, and response to implement the new pagination contract. Must-read facts (include in implementation): [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default] [FACT:response-page-type] [FACT:response-page-value] [FACT:response-page-size-type] [FACT:response-page-size-value]

Requirements and actionable steps:
- Request validation and defaults
  - Enforce request.page as an integer with minimum 1 and default 1 when omitted.
  - Enforce request.page_size as an integer, minimum 1, default 25, maximum 100. (Apply [FACT:request-page-size-default] and [FACT:request-page-size-maximum].)
  - Reject any incoming skip or limit parameters; treat them as not accepted and respond with a validation error.

- Error handling
  - On invalid pagination parameters (e.g., non-integer, page < 1, page_size < 1 or page_size > 100, use of skip/limit), return HTTP 422 with a clear error payload describing the invalid field(s). (Use existing status behavior for invalid requests.)

- Response shape and echoing effective values
  - Add response fields page and page_size to the normal list response. Both fields must be integers. (See [FACT:response-page-type] and [FACT:response-page-size-type].)
  - Set response.page to the effective page used for the query and response.page_size to the effective page_size used; use the exact semantic names effective_page and effective_page_size in code/comments as the values being echoed. (See [FACT:response-page-value] and [FACT:response-page-size-value].)
  - The client relies on these echoed values to update its UI; ensure they always reflect any server-side adjustments.

- Pagination internals
  - Compute the data fetch offset using offset = (page - 1) * page_size. Use the effective page and page_size values when computing offset.

- Behavioral requirements and edge cases
  - Accept page_size = 100 as valid and process normally.
  - Reject page_size = 101 (and any >100) with HTTP 422.
  - If page is omitted, treat as page = 1.
  - Ensure existing semantics for count and empty-page responses remain unchanged; e.g., count scope and empty data list behavior should not be altered by this change.

- Tests to add
  - Unit tests for request validation: missing page -> default 1; page_size default 25; page_size boundary tests (1, 100 valid; 101 invalid).
  - Integration tests verifying the full response includes page and page_size integers with the effective values and that pagination offset is applied to data selection.
  - Tests verifying skip and limit parameters are rejected.

- Deployment notes
  - Bump any API documentation and client-facing docs to show page_size default 25 and max 100, and document that the response will echo page and page_size (integers).

Include the required facts markers in PR descriptions, API spec updates, and tests: [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default] [FACT:response-page-type] [FACT:response-page-value] [FACT:response-page-size-type] [FACT:response-page-size-value].
